value: peak frequency mean 72.96 kHz (SD 0.43, n = 10 bats)
structure: echolocation call (constant-frequency Rhinolophus call of a resting bat)
measurement: peak frequency (PF), mean +/- SD, Table 3 row 'Peak frequency (kHz)', column printed 'R. ferrumequinum n = 10'; column order macrotis, osgoodi, ferrumequinum, affinis, pusillus
method: Materials and methods > Collection of data on morphology, bite force, and echolocation calls: 'The echolocation calls were recorded using an ultrasound recorder (UltraSound Gate 116, Avisoft Bioacoustics, Berlin, Germany) when the bats were resting in a temporary laboratory (5 m × 4 m × 3 m), with the recording microphone aimed at the resting bat’s head at a distance of 30 cm.' (joined from reader pieces; the order of the recorder parenthesis within the sentence is as the reader returned the pieces); 'The sampling frequency was 375 kHz, and the resolution was 16 bits.'; 'Each bat was recorded for at least 1 min' [...]. Measurement of wing parameters and echolocation calls: 'For each individual bat, after removing the first and last syllables of each echolocation call sequence, 15 syllables with a signal-to-noise ratio higher than 40 dB were randomly selected.' (joined from reader pieces); analysed 'on the power spectrogram and oscillogram with Avisoft-SASLab Pro version 5.2.9' 'based on a 1,024 FFT, 100% frame size, and 93.75% temporal overlap'; 'three acoustic parameters, including peak frequency (PF), minimum frequency (Fmin), and maximum frequency (Fmax)'. No sentence says how the 15 syllables were combined per bat (averaging is not printed).
conditions: Wild bats mist-netted at the entrance of Xianren Cave (102°20′E, 24°30′N; Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, Yunnan Province, China, 2,049 m) as they returned, August-September 2017 and 2018 (timed 'To minimize the disturbance to lactating bats'), about 21:00 to 04:00; five rhinolophids coexist in the cave. Age judged 'based on epiphyseal fusions'; 'Once juveniles were identified, they were immediately released in situ.' 'A total of 98 bats were captured in the field', the sentence giving, for this species, '11 R. ferrumequinum (six females and five males)'; the sex split of the echolocation sample in Table 3 is not printed. Table 3 n values (33, 28, 10, 11, 10) against captures (36, 29, 11, 12, 10): the sequencing section says 'six individuals with fewer than 12,000 sequences were removed' (three R. macrotis, one R. osgoodi, one R. ferrumequinum, one R. affinis), which accounts exactly for the Table 3 n values, though the paper does not link the two explicitly; one of this species' captured bats was among those removed, sex not stated. Recordings were made on resting bats in a temporary laboratory, so the value is a resting-bat peak frequency, not a free-flight call; the paper does not say which harmonic was measured. Table 3 caption: 'Results of Kruskal–Wallis (all factors except aspect ratio) and analysis of variance (ANOVA) (aspect ratio) tests' 'examining the variation (mean ± SD) of influencing factors among five bat species.' 'The p-values were adjusted with the Bonferroni correction method for multiple comparisons.' The peak frequency row's last two cells are the Kruskal–Wallis chi-squared (53.59) and the Bonferroni-adjusted p (<0.001) across all five species; no pairwise post hoc test for peak frequency is reported. Same row: R. macrotis 57.88 ± 0.86, R. osgoodi 91.27 ± 0.75, R. ferrumequinum (printed) 72.96 ± 0.43, R. affinis 82.92 ± 1.33, R. pusillus 101.92 ± 1.49 kHz; only the record's own species is filed here.
